OCTOBER FIELD LOG — CAT HEAD AREA, LAKE MARION

This is a retrospective of our firsthand October fishing trips, not a claim that the same fish are holding there today. October's fishing gave us a documented starting point for evaluating the seasonal move into November.

OCTOBER 5 — Our trip produced approximately 240 pounds of catfish, including four fish over 50 pounds. Wind was reported around 7 mph from the north-northeast to north-northwest. These are trip totals, not a lakewide catch forecast.

OCTOBER 13 — Fishing near Cat Head, morning surface water temperature was about 75.7°F. Bait was observed in approximately 10–18 feet of water. The recorded catch included a 6-pound channel catfish and an 8-pound blue catfish, followed by a blue reported around 40 pounds later in the trip.

OCTOBER 21 — Near Cat Head, water temperature ranged from approximately 70.3°F to 72.8°F during the trip. We caught blue catfish weighing approximately 30 and 25 pounds in about 18 feet of water, and later a blue around 40 pounds in approximately 22 feet on an upslope.

WHAT THE LOG TELLS US — During the documented October outings, productive water included bait-related structure and depth changes in the upper-teen to low-20-foot range. The October 21 upslope catch shows why the relationship between contours can matter as much as any single depth. These results document where and how we fished on those dates; they do not establish a current bite at Cat Head or across Lake Marion.

NEXT STEP — November coverage will investigate a new location and compare its contours, bait, water conditions, sonar observations and actual fishing results against this October baseline. Public reports explain the general-area structure and reasoning; exact GPS positions and advanced tactics are available to Master Fisherman Patreon supporters.

DIVERSION CANAL FLOW ASSESSMENT — November 24, 2026 (11:38 a.m. EST)

STATUS: NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. The accessible Santee Cooper operator feed was last updated November 23; daily elevations through November 22 are two calendar days old. November 23–24 elevations are unavailable in that feed. USGS Elloree and Pinopolis monitoring pages returned HTTP 403; individual observation times and vertical datum comparability could not be established.

LATEST OPERATOR DAILY ELEVATIONS (feet): November 22 Marion 74.09, Moultrie 74.03, nominal difference +0.06 ft; November 21 Marion 74.08, Moultrie 74.02, nominal difference +0.06 ft. Both rose 0.01 ft; nominal difference unchanged. These are not verified simultaneous hydraulic head measurements.

HYDRO OPERATIONS: The accessible November 23 operator publication tentatively schedules Jefferies for November 24 and 25 from 4 p.m. to midnight, with St. Stephen not scheduled either day. This supersedes the previously reported November 24 schedule in our commentary, but actual operation and any subsequent schedule changes are unverified. November 22 facility discharge entries: Jefferies 4,810; St. Stephen 0 (units not independently confirmed). Neither is a canal-flow measurement.

INTERPRETATION: The older nominal positive elevation difference is consistent with a possible Marion-to-Moultrie hydraulic tendency if datum and observation times are comparable. Current direction and strength cannot be established from stale readings. Wind setup and operational changes may affect the gradient. No direct canal flow observation was verified; no velocity or discharge rate is claimed. Generation schedules alone do not prove canal flow.

level_analysis: Daily lake-level readings above are published with USGS station timestamps. Review each gauge's vertical datum before comparing Lake Marion and Lake Moultrie. Water movement and reservoir operations require separate verification; elevation alone cannot establish canal discharge.
wind_analysis: The hourly wind forecast above provides broad guidance, but wind exposure varies by fetch, shoreline orientation, gusts and travel route. Check the selected forecast area, recheck conditions before launching, and do not treat a forecast as a measured on-water reading.
temperature_analysis: WATER TEMPERATURE REPORT — Wednesday, November 25, 2026 (8:13 a.m. EST). Primary USGS station pages returned HTTP 403 and neither the instantaneous-values nor continuous-data requests yielded usable observations for 02171000 or 02172002. Current Celsius and Fahrenheit readings, observation timestamps, freshness and 24-hour changes remain unverified. This does not establish a sensor outage. Pineville measures bottom water at one Lake Marion location; Moncks Corner measures downstream tailrace canal water, not Lake Moultrie's surface. Neither represents lake-wide surface temperatures. Seasonal cooling can influence baitfish distribution and blue catfish activity, but without verified measurements no current cooling rate or fish location can be established. Use sonar to check forage around channel edges and adjacent flats rather than assuming fish have moved to a particular depth. Sources: https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02171000/ and https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02172002/ . Conditions: https://atsclakes.com/#conditions .
